questions.question: Ruler of which dynasty built the Kandariya Mahadeva temple in 999?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandela.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ruler of the Chandela dynasty **built the **Kandariya Mahadeva temple** in **999 AD.**
 
• The temple is located in **Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh** and is one of the finest examples of medieval Indian architecture.
 
• The** Chandela dynasty** ruled over a large part of central India between the **9th and 13th centuries.**
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is famous for its intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
• The temple complex consists of several **smaller temples** and is a **UNESCO World Heritage site.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Sunga dynasty** ruled over parts of northern and central India from the **2nd century BC** to the **1st century AD.**

 
 
• They were known for their contributions to** Buddhism and the arts.**
 
 
 
• **The Nanda dynasty** was an ancient Indian dynasty that ruled over the **Magadha region **in the **4th century BC**.
 
 
• They were known for their **military prowess and wealth.**
 
 
 
• **The Gupta dynasty** was one of the most powerful empires in **ancient India, **ruling over much of northern and central India from the **4th to the 6th century AD.**
 
 
• They were known for their contributions to** literature, art, and science.**

questions.question: Cycas and Pinus are which type of plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gymnosperms.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cycas and Pinus** are both examples of **gymnosperms**, which are plants that produce **seeds without enclosing them** in a fruit.
 
• Gymnosperms are typically** woody plants** with **needle-like or scale-like leaves** and are often adapted to harsh environments, such as **deserts or cold climates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pteridophyta **refers to ferns and their relatives, which **reproduce via spores** rather than seeds.
 
• **Thallophyta** is a group of plants that includes **algae and fungi,** which are not closely related to Cycas and Pinus.
 
• **Angiosperms** are flowering plants that **produce seeds enclosed in a fruit**, such as apples or tomatoes.

questions.question: What helps in the cultivation of rabi crops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahawat.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahawat** helps in the cultivation of** rabi crops** as it brings** moisture** to the soil and helps in the** growth of crops.**
 
• Southeast trade winds** do not have** a significant impact on the cultivation of rabi crops as they bring dry air and low humidity.
 
• Westerly jet streams are high-altitude winds that **do not directly **affect the cultivation of crops.
 
• Northwest winds can bring cold and dry air, which can **adversely affect** the growth of crops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahawat** is a local term used in India to describe the** southwest monsoon** winds that bring rainfall to the country from **June to September.**
 
• **Rabi crops** are crops that are sown in** winter and harvested in spring.**
 
• Examples of rabi crops include **wheat, barley, and mustard.**
 
• **Southeast trade winds** are prevailing winds that blow from the **southeast towards the equator.**
 
• **Westerly jet streams** are fast-moving winds that blow from **west to east in the upper atmosphere.**
 
• **Northwest winds** are prevailing winds that blow from the **northwest towards the equator.**

questions.question: The Finance Commission of India submits its report to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** The President of India.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Finance Commission of India **is a **constitutional body** that is set up under **Article 280 **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Its primary responsibility is to recommend the **distribution of tax revenues** between the central and state governments. 
 
• The Finance Commission submits its report to the** President of India**, who is the head of the state and represents the country internationally.
 
• The President of India **appoints the members** of the Finance Commission, and their recommendations are binding on the government.
 
• The Finance Commission's report is an essential document that guides the **allocation of resources** between the center and the states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Ayog** is a **policy think tank **of the Government of India that replaced the **Planning Commission.**
 
• It is responsible for providing** strategic and technical advice** to the government on various policy matters.
 
• The **Finance Minister of India** is responsible for managing the finances of the government, including **taxation, expenditure, and borrowing.**
 
• The President of India is the **head of the state** and the **commander-in-chief of the armed forces.**
 
• The President is elected by an **electoral college **and holds office for a term of **five years.**
 
• The President has the power to appoint various **constitutional bodies** and make appointments to various positions in the government.

questions.question: Which of the following is an output of farming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** crops.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Farming is the process of producing food, fiber, and other products by cultivating crops and raising livestock.**
 
• The output of farming includes various agricultural products such a**s crops, fruits, vegetables, dairy products, meat, and eggs.**
 
• **Crops are the most common output of farming,** and they are grown for various purposes such as food, fuel, fiber, and medicine.
 
• Other outputs of farming include animal products such as milk, meat, and eggs, which are obtained from livestock farming.
 
• Air, water, and machines are not outputs of farming, but they are essential resources and tools used in the farming process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****Air **is a natural resource that is required for the growth of plants and animals. It contains carbon dioxide, which is used by plants during photosynthesis to produce glucose and oxygen. Oxygen is also essential for the respiration of plants and animals.
 
• **Water** is another essential resource required for farming. It is used for irrigation, watering livestock, and processing agricultural products. It is also a habitat for aquatic plants and animals.
 
• ** Machines **are used in farming to perform various tasks such as plowing, planting, harvesting, and processing. They help farmers to increase their efficiency and productivity, and reduce the labor required for manual tasks. Some common farm machines include tractors, harvesters, and irrigation systems.

questions.question: Why was the year 1757 an important year for the English East India Company in India?

options.text: In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Hyderabad by defeating the Nizam in the Battle of Plassey.
In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Madras by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Plassey.
In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Oudh by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Berar.
In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Bengal by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Plassey.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Battle of Plassey.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• The Battle of Plassey was a decisive victory of the British East India Company over the Nawab of Bengal and his French allies on 23 June 1757, under the leadership of Robert Clive. 
 
• The victory was made possible by the defection of Mir Jafar, who was Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah's commander in chief. 
 
• The battle took place at Plassey on the banks of the Hooghly River, about 150 kilometers north of Calcutta and south of Murshidabad in West Bengal.
 
• The battle was preceded by an attack on British-controlled Calcutta by Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah and the Black Hole massacre.
 
• This is judged to be one of the pivotal battles in the control of the Indian subcontinent by the colonial powers. 
 
• British acquired significant concessions for previous losses and revenue from trade.
 
• The British used this revenue to increase their military might and push the other European colonial powers such as the Dutch and the French out of South Asia, thus expanding the British Empire.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

• ​Indian Mutiny, also called Sepoy Mutiny or First War of Independence, was a major uprising in India in 1857–58 against the rule of the British East India Company.
 
 
 
• ​Formation of East India Company
 
 
• ​The East India Company was an English, and later British, joint-stock company founded in 1600.
 
• It was formed to trade in the Indian Ocean region, initially with the East Indies, and later with East Asia.

questions.question: Which among the following festivals is also known as Dala Puja devoted to worshiping the sun is traditionally celebrated by the people of Bihar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Chhath Puja__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chhath Puja:

 
 
• Chhath is a Hindu festival dedicated to the Sun god and his wife Usha in order to thank them for bestowing the bounties of life on earth.
 
• The Goddess who is worshipped during the famous Chhath Puja is known as Chhathi Maiya (also known as Usha, wife of the sun god).
 
• The word Chhath means sixth and the festival is celebrated on the sixth day of the month Kartika of the Hindu lunar Vikram Samvat calendar.
 
• The festival is observed over a period of four days.
 
• The rituals include holy bathing, fasting, standing in water for long periods of time, and offering prayers and food to the setting and rising sun.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Bihula** is a festival celebrated in the month of Shravan by the people o**f Bihar and Jharkhand**.

 
 
• It is dedicated to the** snake goddess, Manasa Devi**.
 
 
 
• ** Madhushravani **is a festival celebrated in the month of **Shravan by the people of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.**
 
 
• It is dedicated to** Lord Shiva and the monsoon season.**
 
 
 
• **Sama Chakeva** is a festival celebrated by the** Mithila commun**ity in Bihar and Nepal.
 
 
• It is dedicated to the love between** a brother and a sister.**

questions.question: Which among the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: The melting point of ice decreases with decrease in pressure.
Spherical Shape of liquid droplets is due to the property of surface tension in liquids.
Evaporation takes place only on the surface of liquids.
Liquids at high altitudes boil at lower temperature due to low atmospheric pressure at high altitudes.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** The melting point of ice decreases with decrease in pressure.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The melting point of ice decreases with a decrease in pressure.__

 __
 
• **The statement is incorrect.**
 
• Melting point of ice decreases with increase in pressure because as pressure increases the molecules of ice try to maintain the ratio by decreasing their volume
 
 
 
• Spherical Shape of liquid droplets is due to the property of surface tension in liquids.__
 __
 
• **This statement is correct.**
 
• Surface tension is the tendency of fluid surfaces to shrink into the minimum surface area possible.
 
• Surface tension causes liquid droplets to take up a spherical shape because a sphere has the smallest possible surface area for a given volume.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation can only take place on the surface of liquids because that is where the molecules with the highest kinetic energy are found.** Only molecules with high kinetic energy are free to escape into the atmosphere.
 
• Liquids at high altitudes boil at lower temperature due to low atmospheric pressure at high altitudes.__
 __
 
• **This statement is correct.**
 
• Boiling occurs when a liquid's vapor pressure equals the external pressure.
 
• At high altitudes, the atmospheric pressure is lower, which means liquids can reach their boiling points at lower temperatures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surface tension** is the property of liquids that causes them to minimize their surface area, resulting in the formation of spherical droplets.
 
• **Evaporation **is a process in which a liquid changes into a gas or vapor phase, and it occurs when the molecules of the liquid gain enough kinetic energy to overcome the intermolecular forces holding them together.
 
• **Atmospheric pressure** decreases with altitude, and this reduces the boiling point of the liquid, making it easier to boil at lower temperatures.
